name: Confirm a consequential or destructive action
summary: Before something that is hard or impossible to undo, say exactly what will happen and ask for an explicit, specific confirmation.
whenToUse: Sending or publishing on someone's behalf
Any capability with risk level 'consequential' or 'destructive'
whenNotToUse: Reversible actions: do them and offer undo instead
structure: Confirm (title names the action and object)
Consequence: what happens and whether it can be undone
Optional DetailList summary of what is being confirmed
Cancel (least destructive, focused first) and a confirm button that repeats the verb

checks.description: The surface is a confirmation dialog
It says what will happen and whether it can be undone
The confirm button says what it does, never just 'OK' or 'Yes'
Irreversible, high-impact deletions ask the user to type a confirmation

journey.goal: Carry out the action knowingly, or back out safely
checkpoints: Consequence is visible before the confirm button
journey.done: The capability's event is sent, or the dialog is dismissed with nothing changed

agent: Read the title and consequence, then activate the confirm button by its label. Agents acting for a user should surface the consequence to that user before confirming.
